correctness.rationale: Exact PS and uniform random-priority procedures yield rational assignment matrices, and object relabeling acts freely on strict profiles. The first-agent-normalized census exhausts all 13,824 representatives of 331,776 four-agent profiles, using two mathematically different exact implementations that agree profile by profile and reproduce the certificate. Sign counts, weighted sum and small-n cases follow from the full histogram. The large-n opposing-sign result is proved by an explicit pair-extension that preserves old allocations and cancels rank shifts, not by extrapolated numerics.

originality.rationale: The primary 2001 paper already treats the n=3 mechanism differences and an n=4 direct-dominance example. The novel assessed conclusion is the complete n=4 exact signed Borda-welfare census, its opposite mean sign versus n=3, the distinction between win frequency and expected magnitude, and an analytic embedding of both signs at every n>=4. A full 2026 same-metric paper supplies bounds and asymptotics but not this finite census. Published exact small-market ordinal-efficiency and stochastic-dominance censuses do not determine Borda comparisons when individual rankings are incomparable. Exact counts from two independently coded algorithms and all known directly comparable theorems were evaluated; remaining potential unpublished finite-table coverage is a risk.
residual_risks: The accessible full 2001 paper already covers the specific three-agent configurations; novelty is restricted to the exact four-agent welfare frequency-and-mean claim.
Exact finite PS/RP average-rank calculations may appear in unpublished tables, software appendices, or sources indexed under different titles.
The 2010 replica-economy article was compared by its available abstract only, not by its complete text.
The 2026 expected-rank preprint directly studies the same welfare objective, so independent bibliographic scrutiny remains valuable.

value.rationale: A direct welfare question on two canonical allocation rules is resolved at the first market size beyond known three-agent mechanisms: the exact four-agent distribution distinguishes the frequency of beneficial profiles from impartial-culture aggregate Borda gain, and flips the average sign between n=3 and n=4. Such a contrast is not a routine deduction from Pareto or stochastic dominance on incomparable profile lotteries; the arbitrary-larger-market embedding shows structural persistence without making a misleading uniform welfare claim.
